Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Beasley
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver
Date: 01/18/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 91 as introduced could increase or decrease the administrative obligations of the Board of Pharmacy by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of disciplinary actions that are sent by delivery or courier service as opposed to certified mail. Further, this bill shifts the administration of the election procedure for nominations to the Board to a third party which would decrease the administrative obligations of the Board and increase the financial obligations of the Board, by an undetermined amount, dependent on the fee charged by the third party to administer the election process.
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs

Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions
Sponsor: Beasley
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver
Date: 02/07/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 91 as passed the Senate could increase or decrease the administrative obligations of the Board of Pharmacy by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of disciplinary actions that are sent by delivery or courier service, as provided by this bill, as opposed to certified mail, as provided by current law. Further, this bill shifts the administration of the election procedure for certain Board positions to a third party, which would decrease the administrative obligations of the Board but increase the financial obligations of the Board by an undetermined amount dependent on the cost to have the third party administer the election process.
Howard Sanderford, Chair
Boards, Agencies and Commissions
